title: Task Negative Sampling Enhanced Graph Few-shot Learning

problem.claim: Graph few-shot node classification addresses node classification with limited labeled data in graph-structured networks.

gap.claim: Existing methods neglect global data distribution and inadequately address inter-class separability.

contributions.claim: TaskNS introduces task-negative samples into graph few-shot meta-training tasks.
TaskNS uses a loss function designed to improve intra-class compactness and inter-class separation with task-negative samples.
TaskNS proposes an h-hop-neighbors-based sampling method that selects structurally close task-negative samples.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe TaskNS as a novel graph few-shot node classification framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four benchmark datasets report average improvements of 4.6% in accuracy and 4.9% in F1-score over state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph few-shot node classification is presented as a response to limited labeled data in graph networks.
Existing episodic meta-learning methods are described as overlooking global distribution and inter-class separability.
TaskNS adds task-negative samples, a separation-oriented loss, and topology-based sampling to meta-training.
The authors report improvements on four benchmark datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework incorporates samples outside the current meta-task and selects structurally close negative samples.

interpretation.claim: Negative examples that reflect both broader distributional context and local structural similarity may provide more informative contrast.

application.claim: When designing few-shot graph classifiers, consider combining cross-task negatives with topology-aware hard-negative sampling.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond the reported graph datasets or task setting.

unknowns: Dataset names and experimental protocol are not specified.
Model architecture and baseline implementation details are not specified.
Statistical variation or independent verification of the reported improvements is not provided.
